headline: Operating Resilience in India Outweighs Persistent European Drag

highlights: Sector Outlook: Cautiously Positive Company Outlook & Guidance: Near-term profitability across all operating regions is guided to strengthen materially in H2FY27.
In India, steel realisations are anticipated to increase by Rs 3,500– 3,600/t QoQ in Q3FY27, comfortably offsetting a guided ~$15/t QoQ rise in coking coal consumption costs.

Capital allocation continues to heavily prioritise high-return domestic assets (>70% of capex deployed in India, generating 27% ROIC) alongside high-margin downstream expansions in cold rolling, colour- coated lines, tubes, and tinplate.
Consolidated leverage remains under check at 2.4x Net Debt/EBITDA, with management comfortable maintaining net leverage within the 2.3x–3.0x band during its peak annual capex cycle of ~Rs 20,000 Cr.

Influxes under pre-March transitional safeguard exemptions caused UK flat steel inventories to swell 60% above normal levels (~865 KT, or ~3 months of consumption), delaying the operational breakeven target toward Q4FY27 as excess channel stocks flush out.

Upstream long-term capacity expansion is anchored by the 4.8 MTPA NINL project (targeting full commissioning by FY30), supported by strategic optionalities at Meramandali and a proposed greenfield facility in Maharashtra.
